title: Blue-Green weight checksum anomaly — canary load failure & remediation notes
content:
Summary:

On 2025-11-04 we observed a degradation in quality for a small percentage of inference requests during a blue-green deployment of model-v2.1 -> model-v2.2. The canary fleet (5% traffic) started returning low-likelihood continuations and occasional decode artifacts. Node-level logs showed model load success but downstream logits were anomalous (near-uniform distributions). Investigation traced the root cause to a partial model weight file being present on a subset of nodes — the model loader did not fail loudly because the file size matched the expected size header, but internal tensor checksums did not match. The partial/bit-flipped weights were produced by a flaky rsync during the blue-green sync step.

Immediate impact:
- Affected traffic: canary fleet (~5% of production) for model-v2.2 across 3 AZs for ~23 minutes.
- Customer-visible impact: observed increase in perplexity for affected requests (measured) and a small but noticeable uptick in customer support tickets referencing 'nonsense completions' for one sandbox customer. No broad production SLA violation because the majority of traffic remained on stable green.

Detection timeline (UTC):
- 2025-11-04 02:08: monitoring Alert: emb-quality-regression (canary, model-v2.2) triggered (4 sigma from baseline).
- 2025-11-04 02:09: SRE on-call (Sofia) acknowledged alert and looked at canary dashboards (latency normal, quality metrics dropping).
- 2025-11-04 02:12: Spot check: sample outputs showed hallucinations and odd token distributions.
- 2025-11-04 02:20: Logs: model-server printed "model load succeeded" but runtime metrics showed KV cache warmups failing and attention scores unusually flat.
- 2025-11-04 02:28: Nodal inspection: three canary instances in us-west2 had mismatched file SHA256 of weights vs. expected manifest.
- 2025-11-04 02:32: Canary traffic shifted back to 0% for v2.2 (manual traffic cutoff) and rollback of canaries to v2.1 initiated.
- 2025-11-04 02:45: Affected instances were cordoned and model files re-verified and re-transferred from the artifact store.
- 2025-11-04 02:55: Canary testing resumed with controlled 1% traffic after verified re-sync.

Root cause analysis (summary):
- Primary cause: rsync job that pushes model weights during blue-green deployment encountered transient network I/O errors causing incomplete writes on several nodes. The uploader process relied on file-size header checks and an in-process manifest update, but did not compute or verify a cryptographic checksum (sha256) atomically after file transfer.
- Secondary factor: model loader logic treats "file open + header match" as sufficient for successful load and does not validate internal tensor CRCs/signatures. This allowed corrupted/partial files to be accepted and the server to continue serving (producing low-quality outputs) rather than failing fast.
- Edge condition: the deployment orchestration retried a subset of pushes but the retry logic incorrectly used a cached artifact path that referenced the partially written file instead of pulling fresh from the remote artifact store.

Why this wasn't caught by canary tests:
- The automated canary sanity scripts validated endpoint liveness and basic tokenization checks but did not verify model-level numerical invariants (e.g., tensor checksum or a deterministic test-suite of logits). The QA harness considered a model load successful if initialization returned without exceptions.

Remediation performed during incident:
- Immediate: cut canary traffic to 0% for v2.2 and incrementally routed requests back to v2.1.
- For each affected node: executed sha256sum /srv/models/model-v2.2/weights.bin and compared to artifact-store manifest; when mismatch found we removed the local file, forced a fresh pull (curl/artifact-client --fresh), and then validated checksum again.
- Restarted model-server process and validated logits with a small deterministic probe set (three fixed prompts).
- Adjusted orchestrator to prefer artifact-store URI over cached local path for subsequent retries.

Post-incident changes (short-term patch):
- Add atomic checksum verification to the model push pipeline: the deploy job will now compute sha256 on the stored artifact and attach it to the manifest before uncordoning nodes.
- Modify node-side model agent to perform a sha256 verification after download and before signaling "model load succeeded" to the orchestrator. If checksum fails, agent will delete the corrupted file and retry up to 3x then report failure to the deployment controller.
- Model loader change: add an optional internal tensor signature check (small, fast CRC across key tensors) to detect silent corruption during load. If signature mismatch, loader exits with non-zero status so orchestration will treat the instance as failed.
- Canary test improvements: extend canary probe suite to include numerical invariants: a deterministic set of 10 prompts with expected top-token probabilities range and a soft-perplexity threshold. Canary rollouts will block if the numerical invariants deviate beyond threshold.

Runbook excerpt (commands and checks for on-call):
1) If alert shows quality regression for canary:
   - ssh to one of the affected canary hosts (via bastion), run: sudo -u modelagent sha256sum /srv/models/<model>/weights.bin
   - Compare to manifest: curl -sS https://artifact-store.redwood/models/<model>/manifest.json | jq -r .sha256
   - If mismatch: sudo systemctl stop model-server; rm -f /srv/models/<model>/weights.bin; artifact-client fetch --uri <artifact-uri> --dest /srv/models/<model>/weights.bin; verify sha256; systemctl start model-server
2) If model-server reports "load succeeded" but outputs look bad: run local probe (python tests/probes/run_probes.py --model-path /srv/models/<model> --cases 10) and examine top-token distributions.
3) To rollback canary traffic: update traffic policy in rollout controller: rolloutctl set-weight --model model-v2.2 --percent 0 && rolloutctl set-weight --model model-v2.1 --percent 100

Monitoring/Alerting changes to implement (owner assignments below):
- Alert: create "artifact-checksum-mismatch" alert (SLO: fire before downstream quality regression) — owner: Priya Rao (infra).
- Alert: canary-numerical-invariant-failure -> will block rollouts automatically — owner: Ravi Patel (SRE).
- Dashboard: add checksum distribution panel and artifact-transfer error rate.

Follow-up action items (owners and ETA):
- Priya: add atomic checksum verification to deploy pipeline and update manifest schema (SRE-4832) — ETA 2025-11-12.
- Ethan: implement node-side checksum verification + 3x retry logic in model-agent and ship in 2.1.3 agent release — ETA 2025-11-09.
- Maya: expand canary probe suite with numerical invariants and create gating rule in rollout controller — ETA 2025-11-08.
- Sofia (on-call lead): update on-call runbook with the ssh/sha256 steps and publish a short playbook for triage — ETA 2025-11-06.

Lessons learned / notes for future rollouts:
- Never trust size/header-only checks for binary artifacts in a distributed push. Use cryptographic checksums that are verified atomically.
- Failing loudly is preferable to silent degradation for model loads. The platform should prefer early failover/backout over serving corrupted outputs.
- Keep a small deterministic probe suite that exercises key numerical properties of new model weights; these catch subtle bit flips or quantization regressions that simple smoke tests miss.

Appendix: example commands used during remediation:
- Verify checksum locally: sha256sum /srv/models/model-v2.2/weights.bin | awk '{print $1}'
- Get expected checksum: curl -sS https://artifact-store.redwood/models/model-v2.2/manifest.json | jq -r .sha256
- Force fresh pull (artifact-client): artifact-client fetch --uri s3://artifacts.redwood/models/model-v2.2/weights.bin --dest /srv/models/model-v2.2/weights.bin --verify false && sha256sum /srv/models/model-v2.2/weights.bin
- Restart service: sudo systemctl restart model-server@model-v2.2

Contact / escalation:
- Primary SRE on-call: Sofia Martinez (pager)
- Secondary: Ravi Patel
- Eng on-call for model packaging: Maya Chen

This document is intended to be living until short-term patches are deployed; once follow-ups are completed we'll produce a final postmortem and move the runbook additions into the canonical SRE runbook repo.
